Production costs can be reduced about 5% when 27% to 45% of LDVs actively respond to prices (TOU and sometimes RTP) and up to about 10% if 45% of LDV charging is scheduled over a week as part of a DLC program. 17 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. 4 Discussion and Conclusions Improved forecasting of price-responsive EVMC increases bulk power system production cost savings and makes price-responsive EVMC on RTP or TOU rates preferable to DLC at higher participation and flexibility levels. On the envisioned ISO-NE bulk power system, perfect- foresight RTP is preferred to DLC with up to 27% of LDVs participating in within-session managed charging, and perfect-foresight price-responsive strategies are value-competitive up to at least 27% and 45% participation for within-week and within-session EVMC scheduling, respectively. Improved forecasting provides more savings as the amount of EVMC flexibility and the time granularity of prices increases. Even with improved forecasting, value can be contingent on the rest of the power system: for example, with 27% of LDVs scheduling charging across the week in response to an RTP forecast, savings can be realized only if generators provide additional operational flexibility to serve increased load ramp rates. We demonstrate that price-responsive dispatch of increasing shares of EVMC can be better achieved with a combination of two strategies: (1) flattening the response through managed TOU and (2) accurate price-response forecasting. Price-responsive managed TOU dispatch could be preferable to more complicated DLC approaches if operational flexibility is difficult to procure, if bulk power systems do not provide multiday schedules and pricing, or if costs of DLC implementation exceed additional savings compared to managed TOU responses. We find that the additional costs of the most valuable mechanisms, which are within-week flexibility exercised via RTP at low participation rates and via DLC at high participation rates, must be less than tens of dollars per vehicle-year, and in some cases can only be a few dollars per vehicle- year, to outperform simpler mechanisms like flattened (managed) TOU and within-session flexibility. Although many North American utilities are still piloting EVMC, Baltimore Gas and Electric’s recently expanded EVMC program forecasts costs of around $50/vehicle-year for incremental participation in 2026–2027, excluding customer participation incentives for a DLC- like implementation with 20,000–30,000 participating vehicles (Michel 2024).
